_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`Verify current Cloudflare Agents / Durable Objects limits and migration constraints:
- CPU time per request
- memory per instance
- schedule/alarm limits per agent/object
- WebSocket connection caps or memory-bound constraints
- SQLite migration behavior and downgrade constraints
Provide official Cloudflare docs URLs and exact current values as of 2026-03-30.`

💡 Result:

## Current limits / constraints (verified against Cloudflare docs on **2026-03-30**)

### CPU time per request (Agents / Durable Objects)
- **Durable Objects invocation CPU (HTTP request, WebSocket message, or Alarm):** **30 seconds by default**, configurable up to **5 minutes of active CPU time** via `limits.cpu_ms`. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/))  
- **Agents “compute time per Agent”:** **30 seconds**, refreshed on each **HTTP request / scheduled task / incoming WebSocket message**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/platform/limits/?utm_source=openai))

### Memory per instance
- **Workers memory limit (applies to Workers and Durable Objects isolates):** **128 MB** (Free and Paid). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/?utm_source=openai))

### Schedule / alarm limits per Agent / Durable Object
- **Durable Objects alarms:** **1 alarm scheduled at a time per Durable Object** (`setAlarm()` overwrites the prior schedule). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Agents scheduling APIs:** implemented “under the hood” using **Durable Object alarms**, so they inherit the **single-alarm-per-object** constraint. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Alarm retries:** exponential backoff starting at **2 seconds**, **up to 6 retries**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Wall-clock time for Durable Object alarm handler invocations:** **15 minutes**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/))

### WebSocket caps / constraints (Durable Objects)
- **Max concurrent WebSocket connections (Hibernation WebSocket API):** **32,768 connections per Durable Object** (practical limit may be lower due to CPU/memory/workload). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/state/?utm_source=openai))  
- **WebSocket message size limit (received frames):** **32 MiB**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/))

---

## SQLite (Durable Objects) migration behavior + downgrade constraints

### Durable Objects “migrations” (class mapping) behavior
- **Migrations are required** to create/rename/delete/transfer Durable Object classes; **code-only changes do not require a migration**, but **you must ensure backward compatibility with stored data**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/))  
- **Migrations are atomic and cannot be gradually deployed** (and Cloudflare states new versions with new migrations cannot be uploaded for early feedback). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Uploading a Worker “version” that includes Durable Object migrations is not supported**; use `wrangler deploy` when applying a DO migration. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/versions-and-deployments/?utm_source=openai))

### SQLite backend enablement / “downgrade” constraints
- **You cannot enable the SQLite storage backend on an existing, deployed Durable Object class** (i.e., adding `new_sqlite_classes` in a later migration will fail). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Workers Paid → Workers Free downgrade constraint (storage backend):** you must **delete all key-value–backend Durable Object namespaces** before downgrading (Free only supports SQLite-backed DO). ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/))  
- **Delete migrations are destructive:** deleting a class **permanently deletes all data for that class**. ([developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/configuration/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Official docs URLs (Cloudflare)
```text

https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/
https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/

https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/versions-and-deployments/
https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/
```

- 2: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/platform/limits/?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/?utm_source=openai

---



</details>

**Correct platform limits and migration constraints against official Cloudflare docs.**

The documented limits contain factual errors:
- **Schedules per agent:** claim of "1000/agent" is incorrect; Agents use Durable Object alarms under the hood, which allow **only 1 scheduled alarm at a time per Durable Object** (not 1000). Retries follow exponential backoff with up to 6 attempts.
- **WebSocket connections:** documented as "no hard cap but memory-bound"; the actual constraint is a **hard cap of 32,768 concurrent connections per Durable Object**, though practical limits may be lower due to CPU/memory.
- **SQLite migration:** claim to "avoid downgrades after SQL migration" is incomplete. You **cannot enable SQLite backend on an existing deployed Durable Object class**—SQLite must be enabled at creation time, not migrated retroactively.

CPU (30s default, configurable to 5 minutes) and memory (128 MB) limits are correct.

Add canonical links to the official Cloudflare docs to prevent future drift:
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/platform/limits/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/

The --ignore-missing-args flag was introduced in rsync version 3.1.0. It ignores missing source arguments (e.g., command-line files or --files-from entries) without erroring, allowing rsync to continue without attempting to transfer nonexistent files. This option does not affect vanished-file errors during transfer. Prior versions, such as 3.0.4 and 3.0.6, do not support it, resulting in "unknown option" errors. The flag is defined in options.c as part of the missing_args handling (1=ignore, alongside 2=delete for --delete-missing-args).
